title: Sahelanthropus tchadensis
summary: Sahelanthropus tchadensis is known from a nearly complete cranium nicknamed Toumaï, found in 2001 at locality TM 266 in the Djurab Desert of northern Chad by a team led by Michel Brunet. Cosmogenic nuclide dating gives about 7.04 million years, and whether it belongs on the human line is debated.

uncertainty.note: Converted as year = 1950 minus age. Cosmogenic dating gives 7.04 +/-0.18 Ma (bounds 6.86-7.22 Ma used here); the Australian Museum gives 6-7 million years.

as_recorded.value: an age of 7.04 ± 0.18 Ma for Sahelanthropus tchadensis
